To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the centrifugation of extended boar semen reduces the proportion of sperm that specifically responds to the capacitating agent bicarbonate, and that this effect is most pronounced in in vitro‐aged samples.

the centrifugation stress of density gradients reduces the ability of sperm to specifically respond to the capacitation stimulus bicarbonate in in vitro‐aged semen, thus reducing the physiological relevance of capacitation assays performed with centrifuged sperm.
centrifugation stress alters the physiological property for controlled capacitation of in vitro‐ aged spermatozoa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of density gradients on sperm physiology.
the impact of sperm centrifugation on sperm capacitation and fertilization.
the impact of centrifugation stress during sperm preparation on the physiological ability of boar spermatozoa in vitro to specifically respond to a capacitation signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the centrifugation stress of the density gradient centrifugations reduces the responsiveness of the spermatozoa in vitro to a capacitation signal.
centrifugation stress reduces capacitation responsiveness of spermatozo to the capacitation stimulus bicarbonate in vitro‐aged semen, but not to calcium influx.
centrifugation stress reduces spermatozoa's capacity for controlled capacitation and increases their ability to respond to incubation per se.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
density gradient centrifugations are not suitable for the evaluation of sperm capacitation in in vitro‐aged samples.
centrifugation of in vitro‐stored boar semen induces a stress factor that alters the capacitation dynamics of spermatozoal subpopulations.
centrifugation of boar semen is a stress factor that alters the physiological response of spermatozoal cells to a capacitating stimulus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
centrifugation stress reduces spermatozoal responsiveness to a capacitation trigger in in vitro‐aged boar semen.
centrifugation stress may reduce the ability of sperm cells to specifically respond to the in vitro capacitation stimulus, bicarbonate.
the centrifugation of sperm cells is a stress factor for the cell, and it can change the physiological property of cells.
